WHAT CHANGES. ehr.prescriptions gains seven nullable columns without default, so no rewrite and every existing row reads null: priority, medication_strength, medication_dose_form, duration_value integer, duration_unit, quantity_to_dispense numeric(12,4) and quantity_unit (the others text), and one CHECK, prescriptions_dispensing_details_ck, added NOT VALID and then validated, so the table is scanned once: priority routine, urgent, asap or stat; medication_strength and quantity_unit not blank and at most 80 characters; medication_dose_form tablet, capsule, liquid, injection, cream, inhaler, drops or other; duration_value 1-3650 and duration_unit day, week or month, both or neither; quantity_to_dispense above 0 and quantity_unit, both or neither (one CHECK for the seven columns, not one per rule, because each VALIDATE CONSTRAINT scans the whole table under the lock; the EHR API checks each rule by name before it writes). One new function, pharmacy.work_item_prescription_details(uuid[]) (md5 e6013d732354a56794ad8ec7f2bbaf0c), plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, not STRICT, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp (every name qualified), owned by pharmacy.work_items' owner, no migration number in its body. For each given work item that is own work (order_route_id null) at the session's facility, whose member holds pharmacy.work-item.read there (auth.membership_has_permission) and passes identity.has_active_consent_grant(patient, subject, membership, facility, 'read_records', the session's purpose), the own-row branch of the work items' read policy (so an emergency session with an active break-glass grant is included, and a revoked, expired or held grant, a deny directive, an inactive membership or a disabled account gives no row), it answers the seven values of the prescription version Pharmacy accepted, read from that version's snapshot in ehr.record_versions (resource_type 'prescriptions', resource_id the prescription id, version_no the accepted version, naming the work item's patient, facility and encounter), so they stay those of the accepted version after the prescription changes. The work item's keys are turned into text in a materialized CTE before the join, so the join compares text with text (texteq is leakproof) and uses the snapshot key (resource_type, resource_id, version_no) under the forced read policy, which then runs once per work item; a join on the uuid cast to text inside it (uuid_out is not leakproof) cannot be an index condition below the policy, which then ran on every prescription snapshot of the item's patient or facility. At most 200 ids, else 22023 WORK_ITEM_PRESCRIPTION_DETAILS_INVALID. The snapshot path was decided by test: ehr.record_versions' only read policy is ehr.context_allows(patient_id, facility_id, 'read_records'), the same facility-and-consent test for an own row, and under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner the suite reads every expected value through it. Nothing is copied into pharmacy.work_items: pharmacy.validate_work_item (0100, e2411539ee8c95a02dad46c03e24db05), pharmacy.validate_dispensing (0101, 17f7e8897bd2ab240332e4d2c9f757b7), ehr.send_order_route (0098's body 4202ba3bbf02abd7db34606d42adca9c, or 0123's 0c2def2b530bcb3d68537ade52787b6b once 0123 is live), ehr.sync_order_routes_on_order_change (0086, 8ce6b42450cc06fc02fec8d1cf63af41) and ehr.capture_record_version (0004's body 70daa16f05bb3ec28f05292e6358a702, or 0112's cae99883d00e70ab1d20ed6fbc97ad7b once 0112 is live) are untouched and checked before and after. No policy, trigger, index, role or other function changes; no existing row is touched. runtime-grants.sql gains a 0125 block: EXECUTE to hid_pharmacy_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, revoked from PUBLIC; the migration grants exactly the same; the EHR runtime's privileges on ehr.prescriptions are table-wide and cover the new columns. Today's images on the new schema answer as before: every writer and reader of ehr.prescriptions names its columns, and the bodies that read the row into ehr.prescriptions%ROWTYPE re-resolve after ADD COLUMN, also in a pooled connection that ran them before (proved: one psql session ran the pharmacy-prescription-source, pharmacy-dispensing-source and order-routes-send suites on 0103 + 0113, the runner applied 0114 (now 0125) from another connection, and the same session ran them and the 0125 suite again, all passing; the 0125 suite also adds a further column in its own session and accepts, dispenses and reads again).
